Arizona Cardinals.longComment: Love must miss at least one more game due to the right high-ankle sprain that he picked up in a Week 8 win at Dallas, but the Cardinals have a decision to make next week, as they have a Week 13 matchup with the Eagles on tap before a Week 14 bye. For as long as Love is sidelined, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will continue to man Arizona's backfield.

Beck continues to deal with back spasms that sidelined him this past Sunday at Kansas City. LaFleur told Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site Wednesday that the team is preparing Josh Johnson to start Sunday's game against the Commanders, so Beck seemingly is in danger of missing a second straight contest.

Simon is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. His absence gives the Cardinals less depth at linebacker behind Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson and Zaven Collins.

Atlanta Falcons.longComment: Pearce was dealing with a back injury in early November but has played in each of the Falcons' last two games. He has two more chances to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's road game against the Vikings.

After being sidelined for the Falcons' previous two games, Branch isn't yet back to full health coming out of a Week 11 bye. The Falcons will see what, if anything, Branch is able to do at practices Thursday and Friday before deciding whether he'll carry a designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings. The rookie third-round pick out of Georgia has been a regular presence on the Falcons' return units but hasn't seen much involvement on offense when healthy; he's recorded 10 catches for 64 yards on 12 targets through his first eight NFL appearances.

Dotson was a spectator for the Falcons' first Week 12 practice along with rookie Zachariah Branch (hamstring), making the activity of both receivers worth tracking the next two days to get a sense of whether either has a chance to play Sunday in Minnesota. Up until the Falcons' Week 11 bye, Dotson has been a picture of health during his first season in Atlanta, appearing in all 10 games while recording 19 receptions for 416 yards and two touchdowns on 39 targets.

Baltimore Ravens.longComment: Madubuike was unable to play against the Panthers in Week 11 due to a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Chargers in Week 10. He would need to practice in at least a limited capacity over the next two days to have a realistic shot at playing against the Texans on Sunday.

The wideout was listed with a calf injury in practice last week, so this is a new one for Bateman. He's mostly been running wind sprints for the Ravens this season, clearing out the underneath routes for Zay Flowers and the tight ends. Bateman is averaging 2.3 catches per game for 36.6 yards with two total touchdowns across 11 contests.

The same applies to fellow starting WR Rashod Bateman (groin), with the duo's status now worth tracking an advance of Sunday's game against the Texans. In Baltimore's 35-33 loss to the Panthers in Week 11, Flowers was on the field for 88 percent of his team's snaps on offense, while recording an 8/97/0 receiving line on a game-high 11 targets.

The Ravens had previously announced that Henry cleared the five-step protocol after being checked for a concussion late in Sunday's 35-33 loss to Carolina. However, Minter noted that the running back later had "a couple of small symptoms" crop up, resulting in him being subject to the protocol as the Ravens kicked off Week 12 prep, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. The fact that Henry was able to practice in some fashion Wednesday indicates that he's already cleared a couple steps of the protocol, but he'll still need to upgrade to full activity and pass neurological tests before he's officially given the green light to play Sunday.

Green continues to be a bright spot for a struggling Ravens team, and he logged two sacks for the second straight contest in Week 11. He might be worth IDP consideration in leagues that award a premium for sacks going into a Week 12 matchup at Houston.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: The linebacker was injured in Week 10 against the Jets and missed last Sunday's victory over Miami. He was able to log a trio of limited practices this week, giving Williams a chance to return from a one-game absence. Williams has piled up 61 tackles (27 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass breakups, including a pair of interceptions, and one fumble recovery across nine games this season.

After being listed as DNP on Monday, Benford was estimated to be a limited participant at Tuesday and Wednesday's walkthroughs. He's looking to return from a one-game absence that forced him to miss last Sunday's win over the Dolphins.

Kincaid, who was inactive for this past Sunday's win over the Dolphins, logged a limited listing on the Bills' Monday through Wednesday practice/injury reports before being deemed questionable to face Kansas City. Per Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard, following Tuesday's practice Kincaid said that he's "most likely playing" Thursday, with the tight end's Week 12 status set to be confirmed once Buffalo's inactives are posted ahead of the team's 8:20 pm kickoff.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: After having his window opened Nov. 11, Brooks was a limited practice participant throughout Week 10 before practicing fully for all three of the Panthers' Week 11 sessions. Brooks is poised to remain a full practice participant leading up to Monday's game at Tampa Bay, but he doesn't appear to be a lock to get activated from IR for that contest. Canales noted that Chuba Hubbard has thrived of late as the Panthers' lead back, while Trevor Etienne is coming off a positive showing as the top complement to Hubbard in this past Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens. Meanwhile, Anthony Tyus has carved out a role as Carolina's kickoff returner, and AJ Dillon looms as a fourth option at running back. Given the crowding in the Carolina backfield along his lack of contribution on special teams, Brooks may need to look impressive in practice this week for the Panthers to justify adding him back to the 53-man roster.

McMillan didn't partake in Wednesday's unofficial practice, after which Canales revealed that the wide receiver dealt with soreness in his foot after Sunday's win against the Ravens in which he hauled in six of nine targets for 71 yards and one touchdown. Considering the Panthers likely are practicing Wednesday in lieu of a session on Thanksgiving, McMillan appears set to be listed as a DNP on the team's first Week 12 injury report Thursday.

Christensen has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury all year, but he was not activated from IR within 21 days of returning to practice, so he'll now miss the rest of the season. The veteran guard will now have to look forward to hopefully returning at some point in 2027.

Horn is currently considered day-to-day, but head coach Dave Canales wants to ensure Horn is in a great head space before returning. The 2021 first-round pick has been sidelined since late September, while Chau Smith-Wade has handled slot-cornerback duties in his absence. The Panthers will still have to officially activate Horn off injured reserve before he's eligible to return.

Chicago Bears.longComment: It's a new injury for Stevenson, who was added to the injury report Wednesday with a limited practice. If Stevenson is unable to play against Detroit, Clark Phillips and Malik Muhammad would be in line for heavy snaps alongside Jaylon Johnson at cornerback.

The cornerback didn't practice at all this week and will miss a second straight game after he was injured in Week 9 against the Bucs. Clark Phillips handled third cornerback duties in last Sunday's win over the Saints.

Johnson injured his ankle in Sunday's win over the Saints, and with the quick turnaround for Week 12, he won't be available against the Lions. The Bears will roll with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai as their only healthy backs for Thursday's game.

Hicks was not listed on Monday's injury report, but he was unable to practice Tuesday due to a concussion. He's mostly played on special teams this season, but his absence thins the Bears' depth at safety behind starters Cam Lewis and rookie first-rounder Dillon Thieneman. Hicks' next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: Davis strung together multiple full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 12, but he still drew the doubtful tag for Monday's game. He'll end up missing a seventh consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to return is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

Iosivas will remain on injured reserve for at least one more week, after the Bengals had listed him as doubtful heading into Monday's contest following a trio of full practices from Thursday through Saturday. If the fourth-year wideout can turn in another full slate of practices in Week 12, he should have a better chance of being restored to the 53-man roster ahead of the Bengals' Nov. 29 matchup with the Saints.

Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: Williams may have picked up the injury during the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans, when he logged nine tackles (five solo) and one pass defense. The injury designation follows the Browns' Week 11 bye, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation ahead of Sunday's game against Las Vegas.

Whiteheart is dealing with a hip issue coming out of the Browns' Week 11 bye, but he'll have two more opportunities to practice in full and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders. The 26-year-old tight end has four catches on seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown through 10 regular-season games.

The Browns are coming out of a bye, so it's unclear whether McGuire picked up the injury during the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans. Regardless, he'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.

Hickman was held out of the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans while in the league's concussion protocol. Cleveland's Week 11 bye gave him extra time to recover, and while his full session Wednesday is encouraging, Hickman would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear protocol and be available to play Sunday against Las Vegas.

Sanders was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he was limited in his first practice session since suffering a hip injury against the Jets in Week 5. He'll have two more opportunities to log a full practice, but Sanders would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Raiders.

The Browns were on bye last week, but it's worth noting that Fannin's reps were also limited Wednesday and Thursday (by the same listed groin issue) ahead of Week 10 action, before the TE logged a full session that Friday, and was then cleared to face Houston. With no reported setbacks in his team's 27-24 win over the Texans on Nov. 15, a game in which the TE recorded a 87 percent snap share, it seems likely that Fannin's Wednesday limitations were maintenance-related.

Prior to a Week 11 bye, Boston was managing a toe injury and missed Wednesday and Thursday practices Wednesday before being a limited participant Friday. Though he had been listed as questionable ahead of the Browns' Nov. 15 game against the Texans, Boston was ultimately active and recorded an 85 percent snap share in a 27-24 win. It's not clear if Boston is still nursing the same toe injury coming out of that game, or if a different health concern is keeping him off the field to begin Week 12 prep.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Locke entered the league's concussion protocol following the Cowboys' Week 9 win over the Colts. He hasn't progressed enough in his recovery to return for Thanksgiving Day and will thus miss a third consecutive game. Locke's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

Mingo's absence for Thanksgiving Day will be his third missed game in a row due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Colts. His absence means KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown will continue to operate in rotational roles on offense behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy. Mingo's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

While he's listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Eagles, Thompson looks likely to play after logging a trio of full practices this week. Thompson has been sidelined since being injured in Week 3. He should reclaim his starting safety job alongside Malik Hooker.

As expected, Ferguson will be sidelined for a third straight game after he failed to practice in any fashion this week while continuing to tend to a pair of lower-body injuries. Brevyn Spann-Ford will be in line for another turn as the Cowboys' top tight end while Ferguson is sidelined. After the Thanksgiving Day contest, the Cowboys will face a longer turnaround for Week 13 with a Dec. 7 matchup against the Seahawks, and Ferguson should have decent odds of making it back for that game.

Moore has logged five-straight full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He would need to be activated from IR in order to be available against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. The rookie fourth-rounder has yet to appear in a regular-season game due to a hip injury that he sustained in training camp.

Bland was placed on injured reserve Sunday after suffering an ankle injury during the Week 10 loss to the 49ers, but the injury is not expected to be season-ending. The earliest Bland will be eligible to make his return is the Week 16 matchup versus Jacksonville, and Ameer Speed and Cobie Durant should continue to see increased playing time in his absence.

Denver Broncos.longComment: Tuesday was Denver's first practice, and given Elliss's absence, he's highly unlikely to participate in any of the Broncos' next two sessions ahead of Black Friday. The third-year linebacker is recovering from an ankle injury that landed him on IR in late October. Assuming he doesn't play in Week 12, Elliss's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Badie was back on the field for Tuesday's walkthrough practice, with Denver estimating him as a full participant, per Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site. Before fracturing his thumb in Week 6, Badie had handled a light role out of the backfield over five appearances, carrying the ball just six times for 22 yards to go with six catches for 67 yards. However, with RJ Harvey (knee) not yet ready to return from IR and with J.K. Dobbins (personal) serving a team-imposed suspension in Week 12, Badie could find himself as the top backup to rookie Jonah Coleman if he gets activated from IR ahead of Friday's game at Pittsburgh.

Detroit Lions.longComment: Clark ended Week 12 prep with a limited practice after starting the week's walkthrough as a DNP. The free safety played 100 percent of the Lions' defensive snaps in Week 11 despite Kerby Joseph's return to the field, meaning an inactive status for Thursday's contest against the Bears would harm the Lions' starting secondary in a significant way.

Wonnum missed two Week 12 prep sessions before participating in the Lions' practice session Wednesday as a limited participant. The defensive end likely picked up his back injury in the team's Week 11 win over the Buccaneers. If Wonnum cannot suit up for Thursday's game, Eric O'Neill and Tyler Lacy will likely see more snaps at defensive end opposite Derrick Moore in the game.

Mays missed the Lions' two prior games due to an ankle injury that he sustained against the Vikings in Week 8. His placement on IR means he's required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against Minnesota. Juice Scruggs figures to be the Lions' starting center for as long as Mays is sidelined.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: Franklin drew the questionable tag for Wednesday's game following three consecutive limited practices. However, the veteran linebacker will end up missing a fifth consecutive game due to a hairline fracture in his shin that he suffered during a practice session in late October, so Ty'Ron Hopper will continue to operate in an elevated role on defense. Franklin's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Coming out of the Packers' Week 11 bye, head coach Matt LaFleur told Matt Schneidman of The Athletic on Saturday that he didn't expect Jacobs to play in Week 12, but he also gave the running back a "chance to prove" he can. Jacobs then was listed as limited on practice reports Sunday through Tuesday and tagged as questionable ahead of Wednesday's game. Such activity wasn't enough for Jacobs to get the all clear to suit up, meaning Green Bay's backfield will be manned by Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks for a second consecutive contest.

LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

Houston Texans.longComment: Rankins sustained an ankle injury during Thursday's win over the Colts and did not return to the contest. The defensive tackle's absence from Wednesday's session suggests the injury was significant. Rankins will have Thursday and Friday's sessions to return to practice in time to avoid an injury designation, or at least have a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Ravens by earning a questionable tag.

Hunter did not play in Thursday's win over the Colts due to his hamstring injury. The defensive end has still not returned to practice since sustaining the injury during Week 10 prep. If Hunter continues to miss practice, he will be in line to miss his third consecutive game due to the injury.

This past Friday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston indicated that the hip injury Boutte suffered in last Thursday's win over the Colts didn't appear to be serious. However, with a 'DNP' to start the practice week, the wideout's status will need to be monitored as Sunday's game against the Ravens approaches. Apart from a 4/125/2 receiving line in a 44-22 win over the Chargers in Week 9, Boutte has produced modest fantasy outputs more often than not, while maxing out at five targets (three times) in 10 contests.

Harrison has been sidelined for the Texans' last two contests, but the WR's ability to practice Wednesday, albeit in a limited fashion, bodes well for his chances of being available for Sunday's game against the Ravens. Harrison's fantasy impact in three outings with Houston since coming over in a trade with Arizona has been modest, so we'd like to see the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft get a full and productive game in before endorsing him as a fantasy lineup option.

Marks didn't practice last week before being ruled out for this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts, but with some extra recovery time since then, the running back is trending toward a return to the lineup Sunday against the Ravens. To get there, however, he'll need to fully progress through the NFL's concussion protocol in the days leading up to the Texans' Week 12 contest.

The Texans announced Rutledge's injury in the waning moments of the contest, but he had been in the medical tent well before that time. Febechi Nwaiwu took over at left guard following Rutledge's departure. With Houston not set to play again until Sunday, Nov. 29, against Baltimore, Rutledge will look to recover from the stinger in time to suit up.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: Taylor-Britt was a full participant in Wednesday's practice in what was his first session since suffering a groin injury in Week 7 against the Vikings. Even if he strings together two more full sessions, Taylor-Britt would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Giants.

Ward missed the Colts' Week 11 game against the Texans due to a knee injury he sustained in Week 10. The cornerback's upgrade to limited participation to start Week 12 prep is a good sign, but he will need to continue logging active sessions for a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Giants.

The tight end has been dealing with a knee issue for the better part of the past month, but Ogletree has continued to play through the injury. Across 11 games this season, Ogletree has four catches for 21 yards on seven targets.

Additionally, Pierce acknowledged that playing in Week 1 was a bit lofty, per Bowen, with the WR saying Wednesday that he was still managing some pain at that stage. In any case, Pierce indicated that he's confident that his current recovery plan will lead to a full return to health. When that will be remains to be seen, but the 2022 second-rounder is still on IR ahead of Week 12, with the Colts presumably not planning to rush him back given the team's 3-8 record in a campaign that's been marked by the team moving several key players ahead of the trade deadline.

In a corresponding move, Indianapolis signed veteran defensive end Carl Lawson from its practice squad to its 53-man roster. Over the first 11 weeks of the regular season, Curry recorded 26 tackles (14 solo) including 1.0 sacks and two fumble recoveries on defense, but most of his snaps came on special teams. He'll have to miss at least the next four games as he recovers.

McGowan went down with the injury while returning a kickoff in the first half of the Week 11 loss. The rookie seventh-round pick had been solidified as the top backup to starting running back Jonathan Taylor, but DJ Giddens now is positioned to serve as Taylor's main understudy for however long McGowan is sidelined. McGowan can be safely ruled out for the Week 12 game against the Giants, though a Week 13 bye could help the 25-year-old back avoid additional absences beyond that.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times Union previously noted that he didn't spot Tuten at at Wednesday's session, and the Jaguars have officially confirmed the running back's absence. Added context regarding Tuten's Week 12 status will arrive via Thursday's injury report, but it's unclear if the team will hold a full-scale practice Thanksgiving day.

Dating back to Week 8, Meyers has been listed on Jaguars injury reports with the ankle issue, but it hasn't stopped him from being available on game days. His limitations Wednesday were most likely maintenance-related after he turned in one his best performances of 2026 in this past Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants. Meyers played 83 percent of the offensive snaps in the loss, finishing with four catches for a season-high 85 yards on 10 targets.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: Though Gray was listed as a full participant on the Chiefs' injury reports both Tuesday and Wednesday, the team's TE2 will nonetheless carry a 'questionable" designation ahead of Week 12 action. With a 10-211-1 receiving line through 10 contests thus far, Gray is only an option in the deepest of fantasy formats, at least as long as Travis Kelce is available.

Though Walker was able to log a limited practice Tuesday, he was listed as a non-participant Wednesday and will wind up missing a third straight contest while he continues to nurse a sore groin. With Walker sidelined, rookie Emmett Johnson is set for another turn as the Chiefs' lead back, with Jaydn Ott serving as his top backup and Nate Carter a possible practice-squad elevation. Given that the Chiefs on are on a short week, Walker -- who last saw game action Nov. 8 -- will have added time to heal before the team's next contest Dec. 3 against the Rams.

VanSumeren didn't practice Tuesday due to a sprained knee that will now keep him out for at least the next four weeks, according to Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site. In six regular-season games in 2026, the fourth-year pro played a majority of his reps on special teams, with just six of 104 total snaps coming on offense.

Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Bowers was sidelined for this past Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos, but he's now practiced in a limited fashion in each of the Raiders' last three sessions. Though the Raiders have a bye looming in Week 13 that would give Bowers more time to recover from his lower-body injuries, Kubiak indicated that the break in the schedule won't be a factor in Bowers' status for this Sunday's matchup with the Browns, per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com. Still, Bowers may need to advance to full practice participation by Friday in order to gain clearance for the Week 12 game.

Keenan went down with a knee injury in the first half, and he will now officially be sidelined for the rest of Week 11. With Adam Butler (concussion) also done for the day, JJ Pegues will handle the bulk of the workload at defensive tackle versus the Broncos.

Butler took a blow to the head late in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end due to a concussion. With Tim Keenan (knee) also done for the night, JJ Pegues is the last man standing at defensive tackle for Las Vegas.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: Tomlinson likely sustained his knee injury in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The defensive tackle will likely need to return to practice by Friday's session for a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

Still did not play in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets due to an ankle injury he sustained in Friday's practice. The cornerback remains sidelined with the issue, leaving Deane Leonard and Genesis Smith as the early options at slot cornerback for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

Henley did not play in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets due to his knee injury. The linebacker has not practiced since sustaining the injury after Week 10. If Henley cannot suit up for Sunday's game, Marlowe Wax and Troy Dye will likely see increased snap shares at inside linebacker next to Del'Shawn Phillips.

The veteran tight end injured his shoulder in last Sunday's loss to the Jets but was able to return to the contest, finishing with two catches for 21 yards on four targets on 41.7 percent of the offensive snaps. It's possible Wednesday was more of a maintenance day.

The running back was injured in last Sunday's loss to the Jets. If Mitchell needs to miss time, it would likely turn this frustrating three-way committee backfield into a more traditional two-man affair, with Omarion Hampton handling early-down work and Kimani Vidal spelling him in passing situations.

Herbert entered the NFL's concussion protocol following this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets, and the QB's pending absence from Wednesday's session gives him two more chances to officially log practice reps before for this weekend's game against New England. In his current absence, DJ Uiagalelei is next up for Los Angeles' signal-caller reps, with practice squad member Jake Browning available for a Week 12 elevation, if needed.

Mesidor suffered an ankle injury during the first half, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In the rookie's absence, Caleb Murphy and Bud Dupree are both candidates to see an increase in opportunities at outside linebacker behind starters Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: Ferguson initially seemed to be making good progress in his recovery from the ankle injury, as the Rams elected to open his 21-day evaluation window Nov. 4. However, Ferguson's activation from IR was delayed after he strained his hamstring shortly after he resumed working out, and he hasn't practiced in more than two weeks. Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve as well as the Rams had hoped and now will require a procedure. Los Angeles will have to proceed without two of its top pass catchers for the remainder of the season, as Puka Nacua recently underwent an MCL surgery that entails an estimated 4-to-5-month recovery timeline.

The Rams have seemingly discounted the possibility of Adams coming off IR for a Wednesday matchup with the Packers in Week 12, while a Week 13 return is more plausible but still sounds like a "long shot," according to Rapoport. Instead, the Rams' Week 14 game against the 49ers on Dec. 13 would appear to be the most realistic target for Adams' return, especially since Los Angeles will effectively have a "mini-bye" ahead of that contest following its Thursday night matchup with Kansas City on Dec. 3. Whenever he's reinstated from IR, Adams should be in store for heavy target shares in the Rams' remaining games after star wideout Puka Nacua (knee) underwent season-ending MCL surgery earlier this week.

Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith as the current healthy wideouts on the team's 53-man roster ahead of next Wednesday's tilt versus the Packers. Nacua, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, is slated to become a free agent in March.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: Wayne has missed the Dolphins' last two games due to a quadriceps injury. He would need to practice in at least a limited capacity over the next two days to have a realistic chance of being available for Sunday's game against the Jets.

Brents was initially diagnosed with a shoulder injury during the Dolphins' Week 12 loss to the Bills. He was tagged with a neck injury on Wednesday's report, and he'll have two more chances to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Jets.
Harrison suffered a hamstring injury in Week 1 that landed him on injured reserve. The fact the Dolphins opted to open his practice window after nine weeks suggests Harrison may be nearing a return.

That said, per Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com, Hafley added that the Dolphins will evaluate the QB's status again depending on how he feels at the end of his minimum required stay on IR. For now, Willis is out for at least three more games, with Kyle McCord currently filling in as 1-9 Miami's starting signal-caller.

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: The knee issue is a new concern for Price, who was anything other than a full participant in practice for the first time all season as the Vikings kicked off Week 12 prep. If Price is able to advance to full activity by Friday, he should be in good position to head into Sunday's game against the Falcons without an injury designation. Price typically sees most of his snaps on special teams when the Vikings receiver room is at full strength, but he's seen his playing time on offense pick up over the past three weeks while Jordan Addison has been sidelined with a thumb injury.

Murray hasn't been available for any of the Vikings' last three games while recovering from a Grade 2 hamstring strain, but his ability to kick off Week 12 prep with a limited showing bodes well for his chances of suiting up Sunday versus the Falcons. The 29-year-old signal-caller has started in each of his prior six appearances this season but will be in line for a backup role once healthy after the Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins on Nov. 10 and immediately installed him as their new starter.

Felton has had increased sway in the Vikings offense the past two games with Jordan Addison sidelined, combining for nine catches (on 17 targets) for 75 yards. Addison is trending toward another absence Sunday against the Falcons, so Felton is in line to continue his elevated role this weekend, assuming he's able to play through his hip injury.

Addison is in recovery mode from the thumb injury that required surgery following a Nov. 15 practice, and he's missed the last two games as a result. While an IR stint has been ruled out for Addison, O'Connell relayed Monday that the wide receiver is "progressing really well" but also isn't expected to play Sunday against the Falcons, according to Goessling. As long as Addison is sidelined, some combination of Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton and Myles Price will operate alongside top WR Justin Jefferson.

New England Patriots.longComment: According to Mike Reiss of ESPN.com, Doubs did individual drills and ran routes against air, suggesting the wide receiver was especially limited after having his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the day. Doubs looks genuinely questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

Coming out of a Week 11 bye, Brown didn't take any reps during the two bonus practices the Patriots held Monday and Tuesday, so it comes as little surprise that he was absent from the team's first official practice of Week 12. Head coach Mike Vrabel has already acknowledged that Brown isn't expected to play Sunday versus the Chargers, but the Patriots will likely wait until after Friday's practice before officially ruling the receiver out for that contest.

The move opens Vera-Tucker's 21-day practice window. The oft-injured offensive lineman went down in the Patriots' Week 6 win over the Jets. Greg Van Roten started New England's last game at left guard.

Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: Emerson was held out of practice during Week 11 prep and did not play against the Bears this past Sunday. His full practice participation indicates that he's progressing through the league's concussion protocol, but he would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to be available for Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

Werner was held out of the Saints' Week 11 loss to the Bears due to a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Panthers in Week 10. Wednesday was his first practice participation since the injury, and he'll have two more opportunities to log a full session and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals.

Johnson was listed as having both hamstring and wrist injuries. He injured the hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Bears but this is the first report of a wrist issue. Head coach Kellen Moore said that Johnson is "day-to-day," according to Terrell. If Johnson does not progress in time for Sunday's game, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp would be the Saints' primary tight end options.

New York Giants.longComment: Phillips appears to have come down with an illness, taking him out of Wednesday's prep session. The cornerback has two Week 12 practices remaining to suit back up as a healthy participant before he would need to receive an injury designation heading into Sunday's game against the Colts.

Carter likely sustained his ankle injury in the Giants' Week 11 win over the Jaguars. The linebacker will need to upgrade to at least limited participation by Friday's practice session for a chance to play in Sunday's game against the Colts. Despite starting the week of prep as a DNP, coach John Harbaugh indicated that Carter should be ready to go for Sunday's contest, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.

Reese likely sustained his back injury in the Giants' Week 11 win over the Jaguars. The linebacker not missing a practice session with the injury is a good sign, but he will likely need to continue stringing sessions together Thursday and Friday to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts.

Likely pops up on the injury report to begin the week as the Giants prepare for their matchup against the Colts on Sunday. He practiced in limited fashion but was held back from a full session. Provided Likely can ramp up to a full practice later in the week, he should be ready for Sunday's contest.

Newsome is expected to undergo surgery for a sprained ankle that he sustained in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. Now that he's on IR, Newsome will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Lions on Monday, Dec. 28. Paulson Adebo is expected to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside cornerback in Newsome's absence.

New York Jets.longComment: Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 18 but was not cleared to play against the Chargers in Week 11. If he can string together full practices over the next two days, then Onyemata would have a good chance of being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Dolphins.

Phillips has been working through an ankle injury over the past couple of weeks, so his DNP on Wednesday's report doesn't come as much of a surprise. The veteran defensive tackle will have two more chances to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Dolphins. Phillips has accumulated 42 tackles (16 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one fumble recovery across 11 regular-season games.
The defensive lineman was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Sweat hasn't played since Week 7 and has logged 17 tackles (five solo) across 229 defensive snaps this season.

Though Williams and fellow wideout Omar Cooper (ankle/groin) were both sidelined for the Jets' Week 11 win over the Chargers, the former appears to be in a better spot on the health front to begin Week 12. Williams was able to take some reps in Wednesday's walkthrough session, while Cooper was a spectator. If he's able to play Sunday in Miami and if Cooper remains out for another game, Williams could end up serving as the Jets' No. 3 wideout behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell.

The rookie wide receiver will be sidelined for a fourth consecutive practice while he continues to manage a pair of injuries, but the Jets aren't closing the door on Cooper putting an end to a one-game absence and playing this Sunday in Miami. In order to put himself in a position to suit up this weekend, however, Cooper will likely need to put in a full practice either Thursday or Friday. If Cooper ends up missing another game, the likes of Adonai Mitchell, Isaiah Williams (ribs), Tim Patrick and practice-squad member Sterling Shepard could be in line for added snaps and targets.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: After his trade to the Bengals fell through two weeks ago, Ebiketie is now dealing with an injury that will sideline him for at least one contest. Jalyx Hunt and A.J. Epenesa should soak up extra snaps off the edge for the Eagles.

The cornerback was injured in last Sunday's win over the Steelers. With Jones set to miss Thanksgiving Day against Dallas, Riq Woolen and Kelee Ringo are likely to see increased snaps opposite Quinyon Mitchell.

Baun was held out of practice all week due to a back injury that he sustained against the Giants in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to require a stint on IR, which means he'll miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Seahawks. Jeremiah Trotter figures to start alongside Jihaad Campbell at inside linebacker moving forward, beginning with Sunday's home tilt against the Steelers.

Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Wicks sustained the foot injury Friday, and it presumably led to his placement on IR. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Elliott was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a knee injury to play against the Eagles in Week 11, when he played 22 snaps (14 on defense, eight on special teams) while not showing up in the box score otherwise. Even if he's cleared to play Friday against the Broncos, Elliott would likely operate in a rotational role in the secondary behind Jalen Ramsey, Jaquan Brisker and Robert Spears-Jennings.

Pittman also logged a full participation listing one day before, but the Steelers held a walkthrough practice Tuesday, so Wednesday's session is more relevant with regard to the WR's availability for Friday's game against the Broncos. If Pittman -- who last saw game action in Week 4 -- is activated to face Denver, he'll be catching passing in Week 12 from Mason Rudolph, with the Steelers slated to let veteran signal-calller Aaron Rodgers go.

Dunker has put together four consecutive full sessions since being designated to return from injured reserve this past Wednesday. The rookie third-rounder is in the final stages of his recovery from an MCL sprain that he sustained in September. Dunker would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Friday's game against the Broncos.

Herbig upgraded his DNP practice status from last week to limited participation Tuesday. The 25-year-old missed Week 11 due to a hip injury. He has two more practice sessions to increase his chances of playing Friday against the Broncos.

The 29-year-old appears to have suffered a setback with his calf injury, as he opened Week 12 as a non-participant in practice Tuesday. Skowronek missed the Steelers' last three games due to the same injury. He will likely need to upgrade his practice status for a chance to play Friday against the Broncos.

Highsmith recorded a pair of sacks across just six snaps before he was forced out in the first quarter of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles due to the ankle injury. Per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com, the Steelers' initial belief is that Highsmith's ankle injury isn't serious, but the edge rusher will nonetheless have difficulty getting clearance to play on a short week. If healthy, Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) -- who was inactive for Week 11 -- will be the most likely candidate to start in place of Highsmith on Friday.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: Okuayinonu suffered a broken foot in practice ahead of Week 1 and required surgery. He appears to be making progress and could return at some point before the end of the regular season. The 28-year-old appeared in 15 regular-season games last season, and made 12 starts and recorded 23 tackles (16 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.

Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

After a three-game (and four-week) absence due to right Achilles tendinitis, Evans returned to action during Sunday's win against the Vikings in Mexico City, recording a 43 percent offensive snap share and gathering in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown. The 49ers likely are managing Evans' workload to begin Week 12 prep, but his status nonetheless will be monitored in advance of Sunday's contest against the Seahawks.

Purdy put on a master class during this past Sunday's 35-10 win against the Vikings in Mexico City, completing 21 of 26 passes for 255 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. Now with a health concern in tow, his status will be monitored closely to get a sense of his odds to suit up Sunday against the Seahawks. Mac Jones is waiting in the wings in the event Purdy isn't able to play in Week 12.

Lenoir played in Week 11 despite working through a foot injury that was sustained in Week 9 against Las Vegas. The issue didn't seem to slow the 27-year-old against the Vikings, as he played 81.0 percent of defensive snaps, which was within his usual range.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: Nelson underwent a minor procedure on his knee in early November and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. He's had additional time to rest thanks to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, and Macdonald relayed Wednesday that the team is "hopeful" that Nelson will be cleared to return for Week 13 against the Cowboys on Monday, Dec. 7. Greg Zabel will likely start at left guard in Nelson's absence.

Per John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Wednesday that Lucas is not a candidate for injured reserve but is expected to miss "days to weeks" due to an ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 10 against the Raiders. Josh Jones, Bobby Hart and Chase Lundt are all candidates to start at right tackle for as long as Lucas is sidelined.

Smith-Njigba previously has been listed on Seattle injury reports this season for rest purposes, but this marks the first time his practice reps were impacted by a health concern. He'll have two more days to increase his activity level this week, with Friday's practice report set to reveal if he has a designation for Sunday's game at San Francisco.

Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: McMillan will be back at practice Wednesday for the first time since Week 3, after he was diagnosed with a PCL sprain in his left knee following his early exit in the Buccaneers' Sept. 27 loss to the Vikings. The Buccaneers will have a 21-day window to evaluate McMillan for a return to the 53-man roster, so he won't be a lock to suit up Monday versus the Panthers, even if he's a full practice participant throughout the week. Whenever he's reinstated, McMillan will likely be called upon to fill a depth role behind the Buccaneers' top two receivers, Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin.

Simmons played 17 defensive snaps in Sunday's loss but did not appear in the box score. The defensive tackle has now entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact football activities.

Both Morrison and Jacob Parrish (back) were injured in Sunday's loss to Detroit, forcing Tampa Bay to dip into its cornerback depth. Kevin Knowles picked up the extra snaps opposing Zyon McCollum, with Keionte Scott covering the slot.

Parrish exited Sunday's Week 11 game against the Lions after sustaining a back injury. The 22-year-old has played in nine games in 2026, recording 40 tackles (33 solo) and 14 pass deflections, including two interceptions.

Tennessee Titans.longComment: Flott exited the Titans' Week 11 loss to the Jaguars early with a neck injury and did not return to the contest. The cornerback remains sidelined due to the recent injury, and it remains unclear how much time he is expected to miss. Flott will need to upgrade his practice participation by Friday to have any shot at playing in Sunday's divisional contest with the Jaguars.

Franklin-Meyers played 42 percent of the Titans' snaps in the Week 11 loss to the Cowboys, close to his regular snap share, while playing through a back injury. The defensive tackle will likely continue to practice through the issue in a limited capacity before suiting up for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

Moore may have picked up the injury during the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. James Hudson figures to take over at left tackle in Moore's absence.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Burks presumably had his reps capped for maintenance purposes, as the wideout was sidelined for the Commanders' Week 9 loss to the Rams due to the same foot issue before suiting up in the ensuing two contests. In both of those games, Burks played north of 60 percent of the offensive snaps while producing a combined 4-57-0 receiving line on six targets. Provided he advances to full practice activity by Friday, Burks should head into this weekend's game in Arizona without a designation.

Diggs was away from the team for Wednesday's session due to a personal issue. There's no indication this will be a long-term absence, and the Commanders did excuse him for Wednesday. Still, Diggs' return to the team will be worth monitoring over the coming days in advance of Sunday's game at Arizona.

Robertson suffered an ankle injury at the team's final practice of the week, so his absence Monday comes as no surprise. In his absence, Mike Sainristil and Quan Martin will both likely operate in more prominent roles at cornerback versus Cincinnati.

Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.
